name: Sheva (David's state scribe (secretary))
title: David's State Scribe
summary: Sheva (also known as Seraiah, Shisha, or Sheva) served as state scribe and secretary during King David's reign. He was a key official in David's administration, responsible for official correspondence and documentation. His role testifies to the organized governance that David established in the united kingdom of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as State Scribe under David
keyEvents.description: Sheva is mentioned as state scribe in the list of David's chief officials, reflecting the organized administration of David's kingdom.

keyEvents.title: David's Officials in 2 Samuel
keyEvents.description: In a parallel list of David's officials, the scribe is named Seraiah, which is considered an alternative spelling for Sheva.

keyEvents.title: Part of David's administrative apparatus
keyEvents.description: Sheva served alongside other prominent officials such as Joab (commander-in-chief), Jehoshaphat (recorder), Zadok and Abiathar (priests), and Benaiah (leader of the bodyguard).

keyEvents.title: Parallel in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: In Chronicles, David's royal secretary is mentioned by the name Shisha, confirming the importance of this office in David's administration.

keyEvents.title: Predecessor to Solomon's administration
keyEvents.description: The role of royal secretary that Sheva held under David was continued under Solomon, where his possible sons Elihoreph and Ahijah served as scribes.
